themes_detail.label: Homeless Assistance Requests Surge
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance complaints spiked to 4 this week, a 233% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 1.2 per week, suggesting a sudden concentration of encampments or crisis situations in Brownsville/Ocean Hill requiring immediate intervention.
evidence: 4 homeless person assistance complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.16)
Represents 233% spike from baseline in the most recent reporting period
Highest recency urgency among all spikes in the dataset
reporting_angles: Ground reporting on specific encampment locations and what triggered the sudden uptick
Interview with NYPD, DHS, and outreach teams about resource deployment and capacity

themes_detail.label: Dead Animals Piling Up
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints reached 3 last week, a 243% spike over the 8-week average of 0.9 per week, indicating potential disease vectors, sanitation failures, or wildlife management issues requiring immediate public health attention.
evidence: 3 dead animal complaints last week vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.43, highest z-score in dataset)
243% increase represents nearly 3x normal baseline frequency
High statistical significance suggests anomalous pattern, not random variation
reporting_angles: Partner with NYC Department of Health to determine if there's a disease vector or wildlife outbreak
Check whether DSNY (Sanitation) is responding adequately to these complaints

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Epidemic Cooling
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints peaked 3 weeks ago at 63 (221% above the 19.6 weekly average), though recency is lower; vehicle noise also spiked 3 weeks ago at 17 complaints (249% above baseline), suggesting a recent but now-cooling pattern potentially tied to specific events or enforcement gaps.
evidence: Street/sidewalk noise: 63 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 19.6 weekly average (z-score: 4.21)
Vehicle noise: 17 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 4.9 weekly average (z-score: 5.12)
Both spikes occurred 3 weeks ago; current week data not yet reported to show if trend has reversed
reporting_angles: Investigate what triggered the noise spike 3 weeks ago—local events, construction, or enforcement lapses
Interview NYPD about decibel enforcement and response rates during the peak period

themes_detail.label: Building Access & Window Failures
themes_detail.summary: Door and window complaints jumped to 30 two weeks ago, a 56% increase over the 19.2 weekly average, indicating potential structural deterioration, inadequate maintenance, or break-ins concentrated in a subset of buildings.
evidence: 30 door/window complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 19.2 weekly average (z-score: 3.76)
56% spike suggests concentrated building maintenance failures or security issue
Part of broader housing quality signal alongside paint/plaster and plumbing complaints
reporting_angles: Map complaints to identify if specific buildings or blocks are repeat offenders
Determine whether complaints are security-related (break-ins) or maintenance-related (frames, weatherproofing)

themes_detail.label: Street Maintenance Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or facility complaints spiked to 12 three weeks ago, a 317% increase over the 2.9 weekly average, paired with a 260% spike in street sweeping complaints (9 vs. 2.5 average), indicating possible sanitation service reductions or accelerated street degradation.
evidence: Maintenance/facility complaints: 12 three weeks ago vs. 2.9 weekly average (z-score: 4.5)
Street sweeping complaints: 9 three weeks ago vs. 2.5 weekly average (z-score: 3.15)
Both spikes occurred simultaneously 3 weeks ago, suggesting coordinated service failure or policy change
reporting_angles: File FOIL request for DSNY service logs to see if street sweeping was reduced 3-4 weeks ago
Interview sanitation union and city officials about staffing or scheduling changes in CD316
